content: [tt-mlir](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir) is Tenstorrent's open-source MLIR compiler stack. It handles lowering from TTIR (their high-level ML IR) down to TTNN (their hardware runtime), making decisions along the way about [memory layout](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/636a8c1f9a287970a9123c17fa473249978fd097/lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp#L317), [how tensors are sharded across cores](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/636a8c1f9a287970a9123c17fa473249978fd097/lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp#L91-L97), and [tiling](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/636a8c1f9a287970a9123c17fa473249978fd097/include/ttmlir/Dialect/TTNN/Types/Types.h#L12-L13). I've been wanting to get involved in a serious compiler project for a little while, and scrolling through issues, I found a small, well-scoped ticket which happened to be unclaimed.

[Issue #8322](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/issues/8322) documents a crash: compiling any operation on a rank-0 scalar tensor (e.g. a `tensor<f32>` with no dimensions, just a bare scalar value) blows up when optimization is enabled.

```
ttmlir-opt: /opt/ttmlir-toolchain/include/llvm/ADT/ArrayRef.h:157:
const T &llvm::ArrayRef<long>::back() const [T = long]:
Assertion `!empty()' failed.
```
The minimal case to get a repro was a scalar add:
The issue noted that at `optimization_level=0` (no optimizer passes, direct lowering) the same program compiled and ran fine, and that the crash appeared at level 1.

`ArrayRef::back()` is LLVM's bounds-checked accessor for the last element of an array. It carries the same semantics as a standard `std::vector::back()`, just on an `ArrayRef`. The stacktrace pointed to [ArrayRef.h:157](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/9a6b20fa7ae8bd0a512612f83b0c0a0b9566810b/llvm/include/llvm/ADT/ArrayRef.h#L155-L159):
MLIR APIs like `op.getOperands()` and `op.getResults()` hand you an `ArrayRef`. Tensor shapes are `ArrayRef<int64_t>`, meaning any `shape.back()` call on a rank-0 tensor hits that `assert(!empty())`.

```
$ grep -rn "shape.back()" lib/Dialect/TTNN/ --include="*.cpp"
lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp:781:      int64_t cols = (shape.back() + TILE_WIDTH - 1) / TILE_WIDTH;
lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp:783:          (outputType.getNumElements() / shape.back() + TILE_HEIGHT - 1) /
lib/Dialect/TTNN/Transforms/Decomposition/DistributedRMSNormDecompositionRewritePattern.cpp:32:  if (shape[shape.size() - 2] != 32 || shape.back() % 32 != 0) ...
```

`MemoryLayoutPropagation` is an analysis pass that only runs under [the optimizer](https://docs.tenstorrent.com/tt-mlir/specs/ttnn-optimizer.html), which immediately explained the level-dependent behavior. At level 0 the optimizer doesn't run, so this code never executes.
Tenstorrent devices have a two-level memory hierarchy. From [the TTNN optimizer docs](https://docs.tenstorrent.com/tt-mlir/specs/ttnn-optimizer.html):

L1 is fast, on-chip SRAM local to each Tensix core (~1.5 MB per core). DRAM is slow, shared, accessed over the NoC. `MemoryLayoutPropagation` decides which tensors live where, and how they are sharded across the core grid. The crash is inside [`addReshardCandidates`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/7f37cd1fbd0b18d3b58ab3f1973ffb8a7b0eced0/lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp#L748-L752):

```cpp
void MemoryLayoutPropagation::addReshardCandidates(
    std::vector<InputCandidate> &candidates, Operation *op, unsigned operandIdx,
    Value operand, TTNNLayoutAttr currentLayout, RankedTensorType tensorType,
    const llvm::SmallVector<BeamCandidate, 0> *producerBeam,
    Operation *producerOp, size_t resultIdx, size_t maxCandidates);
```

This function generates candidate memory layouts for each tensor operand in the compute graph. When [the optimizer](https://docs.tenstorrent.com/tt-mlir/specs/ttnn-optimizer.html) is deciding how to shard data across Tenstorrent cores, it calls this to enumerate possible resharding options for each edge. Tenstorrent hardware tiles tensors into 32x32 blocks (`TILE_HEIGHT = TILE_WIDTH = 32`), and a central heuristic in this function is `maxGridVolume`, a cap on how large a grid the reshard is allowed to target.
[Here's the full block that computes it](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/7f37cd1fbd0b18d3b58ab3f1973ffb8a7b0eced0/lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp#L793-L811):

`shape.back()` gets the last dimension: the column count.
- `tensor<64x128xf32>`: shape *-->* `[64, 128]`, `shape.back()` *-->* 128
- `tensor<f32>`: shape *-->* `[]` *-->* `<err>`

Calling `back()` on an empty `ArrayRef` is the assertion failure.

Once `maxGridVolume` is computed, it gets passed downstream to [`generateReshardCandidates`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/7f37cd1fbd0b18d3b58ab3f1973ffb8a7b0eced0/lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp#L1021-L1034), where it's used to filter out grids that are too large:
The crash happens before any of that filtering. It happens during the `maxGridVolume` computation itself, when the output is a scalar and `shape` is empty.
I added a rank guard to the [condition](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/7f37cd1fbd0b18d3b58ab3f1973ffb8a7b0eced0/lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp#L802-L811):

For rank-0 tensors, the block is skipped entirely and `maxGridVolume` stays at `std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max()`. Scalar tensors don't have tiles, so the heuristic doesn't apply to them and leaving the cap unconstrained is the right behavior.
The fix itself was easy. Validating it is where I made three faulty assumptions.
First assumption: since the issue reports a crash at `optimization_level=1`, the test should run at level 1. I appended `@scalar_add` to the preexisting `ttir_to_ttnn_pipeline.mlir` file:

The reviewer came back with:

> *This test won't exercise your fix because you need optimization_level=2 to go through MemoryLayoutPropagation. Please transfer the test into test/ttmlir/Dialect/TTNN/optimizer/ and add a few more ops into the func so that reshard exploration is triggered.*

The test passed because the pass containing the crash never ran. Nice to see green, but this was a false positive. On a side-quest to learn how the pipeline actually gates on optimization level, I found the relevant code in [`resolveOptimizationLevelOptions`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/7f37cd1fbd0b18d3b58ab3f1973ffb8a7b0eced0/include/ttmlir/Dialect/TTNN/Pipelines/TTNNPipelines.h#L516-L537):

`optimizerPassEnabled` gates at level 1. `memoryLayoutAnalysisEnabled` (what actually enables `MemoryLayoutPropagation`) gates at level 2. The issue's reproducer used a real system descriptor, which may enable different behavior at level 1. But importantly, on the mock device, level 2 is required to activate `MemoryLayoutPropagation::addReshardCandidates(...)`. Some might call this tribal knowledge, others might call it self-documenting code - I'm inclined to agree with the latter crowd, but either way, I lazy-loaded this information. This raised the next question: could I even reproduce this without a physical device?
Second assumption: reproducing this requires real hardware.

I told him something along the lines of "I'm happy to repro if I could get early TT cloud access", not entirely without ulterior motive. Turns out, the crash reproduces on the mock device, as long as you're at level 2: **no TT hardware needed**. My no-longer-clever offer to purchase compute came approximately twenty-five seconds prior to this epiphany.

I moved the test to a [dedicated file](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/blob/7f37cd1fbd0b18d3b58ab3f1973ffb8a7b0eced0/test/ttmlir/Dialect/TTNN/optimizer/scalar_tensor.mlir), switched to `optimization_level=2`, and chained four scalar adds to give the reshard exploration enough edges to actually reach `addReshardCandidates`:

I pushed the updated test. The critical checks passed, but CI was red on a few perf tests - almost certainly unrelated to my changes. CI also flagged 0% patch coverage because `// REQUIRES: opmodel` skips the test when `-DTTMLIR_ENABLE_OPMODEL=ON` isn't set, meaning the two new lines never executed in the coverage run.
Third assumption: CI compute budget is infinity, no approval needed.

When CI fails for reasons seemingly unrelated to my diff, my occasionally misguided inner-monologue tells me to merge from main and give the slot machine of CI yet another spin. Transient issues have a way of working themselves out (otherwise, they wouldn't be transient). What I didn't know: in this repo, each merge of `main` into a community contributor's branch re-triggers workflow approval, meaning a maintainer has to manually re-approve every single time. [He asked me to stop.](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/pull/8525#issuecomment-4584493495) Fair enough.
To gain confidence in the guard, I checked out `main` and ran the test 2 ways, side-by-side:

```
$ git checkout main -- lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp \
  && cmake --build build --target ttmlir-opt 2>&1 | tail -3 \
  && llvm-lit -av test/ttmlir/Dialect/TTNN/optimizer/scalar_tensor.mlir
Assertion `!empty()' failed.
Failed: 1 (100.00%)

$ git checkout fix/8322-rank-0-scalar-crash -- lib/Dialect/TTNN/Analysis/MemoryLayoutPropagation.cpp \
  && cmake --build build --target ttmlir-opt 2>&1 | tail -3 \
  && llvm-lit -av test/ttmlir/Dialect/TTNN/optimizer/scalar_tensor.mlir
Passed: 1 (100.00%)
```

The reviewer approved and the PR merged as squash commit [`1ead25f`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-mlir/commit/1ead25fea) into `main`. Suddenly, contributing to the Tenstorrent compiler stack is no longer mysterious.
